faq.q: Did Florida Amendment 3 pass in 2026?

faq.q: What does Florida Amendment 3 do?
faq.a: It raises the homestead exemption for non-school property taxes from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028, then adjusts it for inflation. It also lowers the yearly assessment cap on non-homestead property from 10% to 5% and directs local governments to spend property tax revenue on purposes such as public safety, education and infrastructure.

faq.q: When does the Amendment 3 homestead exemption take effect?
faq.a: The $150,000 exemption applies to the 2027 tax year and the $250,000 exemption to 2028. Most homeowners will first see it on the property tax bill that arrives in November 2027.

faq.q: Does Amendment 3 lower school property taxes?
faq.a: No. The larger exemption applies only to non-school property taxes. School district taxes are not affected.

faq.q: How can I estimate my Amendment 3 savings in Palm Beach County?
faq.a: The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser's Office offers an Amendment 3 calculator on pbcpao.gov where homestead owners enter their address. Savings depend on your assessed value and local non-school millage rates, which can change each year.

faq.q: I'm moving to Florida. Do I get the new exemption?
faq.a: People who were not Florida residents on Dec. 31, 2026 get the current exemption when they first qualify, and the larger exemption starting in their fifth year, according to News4Jax.

faq.q: When is the homestead exemption deadline in Palm Beach County?
faq.a: March 1. You must qualify as of January 1 of the tax year and apply by March 1 of that year. Under Florida law, missing the March 1 deadline means you lose the exemption for that year.

faq.q: How much does the homestead exemption save in Palm Beach County?
faq.a: The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser says it generally saves $750 to $1,000 a year in property taxes. It also limits increases in your home's assessed value to 3% a year or the change in the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower. Amendment 3 raises the non-school exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028.

faq.q: How do I apply for homestead in Palm Beach County?
faq.a: You can apply online through the Property Appraiser's E-File system on pbcpao.gov, in person at a Property Appraiser service center (the closest to Wellington is at 200 Civic Center Way, Suite 200, Royal Palm Beach), or by mailing a printed application.

faq.q: What documents do I need for homestead in Palm Beach County?
faq.a: Social Security numbers for all applying owners and their spouses, a Florida driver's license or ID, proof of permanent residency if you're not a U.S. citizen, and at least one more proof such as a Florida vehicle registration, Florida voter registration, Declaration of Domicile, federal tax return or utility bills for the home.

faq.q: Do I have to reapply for homestead every year?
faq.a: No. Once you qualify, the exemption renews automatically each year as long as you still qualify, and you'll get a pink and white receipt card in late December. You must file a new application if you move to a new home.
